item.title: 90/100 Mixed Use Project / 5468796 Architecture
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: On a long parcel at the edge of Winnipeg's East Exchange District, 90/100, named for its address, unites a 1905 warehouse with a seven-storey contemporary volume to create a medium-density, mixed-use development. Containing 206 residential suites spanning new and old buildings and 6000 square feet of commercial space, the project establishes a deliberate counterpoint to the area's conventional, opaque residential buildings through careful choreography of massing, open space and glazing, rendering the building physically and symbolically open. It strikes a rare balance contributing to the urban fabric, establishing a landmark distinguished by bold geometry and material precision.

item.title: Finishing
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: Obra Blanca is an essential experience for professionals in the architecture finishes and design products sector, including ceramics, bathroom furniture, faucets, lighting, and more. It offers a unique opportunity to scale projects and achieve new objectives by interacting and connecting with suppliers, professionals, and industry leaders.

item.title: Pavilion in Brolo Park / CN10 architetti
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: The construction of the new pavilion is part of a larger urban project to reclaim and enhance a large green space called PARCOBROLO, which extends to the southern part of the town of Bonate Sotto in the Villa district, covering an area of over 30,000 square meters. This large orchard (brolo) has survived over time, untouched by the expansion of the surrounding buildings.

item.title: Public Interest Design in South Africa
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: This book presents salient examples of architectural projects and practices in South Africa since 1994 that collectively subscribe to the paradigm shift towards Public Interest Design. Despite radical political transformation in the country, the people of South Africa remain adversely affected by the socio-spatial legacies of a segregated urban landscape. The contributions by architects to address these challenges go largely unnoticed and remain a marginalised practice, even within the mainstream profession.

item.title: Call for Proposals: Bahrain Pavilion at the Venice Architecture Biennale 2027
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: The Bahrain Authority for Culture and Antiquities invites individuals and collaborative teams to submit proposals to represent the National Pavilion of Bahrain at the 20th International Architecture Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, taking place from 8 May to 21 November 2027, with pre-opening on 6 and 7 May.

item.title: Metaxis: A Collection of Ideas and Objects by FUTUREFORMS
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
This exhibition takes as its point of departure the Greek word metaxi, referring to an in‑between condition—belonging to two realms at once. METAXIS explores what happens in between: between ideas, objects, spaces, and ways of seeing. It reflects on the dynamic state of being in the middle of things, a shifting tension or oscillation rather than a fixed condition. The exhibited projects move fluidly between perception and imagination, inside and outside, presence and absence, art and architecture. What does it mean to create public art and architecture in the 21st century?

item.title: Cinema Studio Namibe: Reviving a Tropical Modernist Icon in Angola
item.dc:creator: Camilla Ghisleni
item.description: What sustains the purpose of architecture that has never been occupied? For decades, this was the question surrounding the Namibe Cinema-Studio, built on the coast of Angola in 1973. Conceived as a film screening venue, the building remained closed and abandoned, never fulfilling the role for which it was created. Yet it withstood the passage of time, becoming an icon of the Angolan landscape and architecture, until finally screening its first film nearly fifty years later.

item.title: The House of Memories / Studio Lagom
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: The House of Memories is born from the desire to move ahead with the times and satisfy dynamic requirements, while enshrining familial memories and celebrating its roots. It is located on a 165' x 55' plot in Valsad, a city filled with beautiful farmland and lotus ponds that make a beautiful inclusion in this narrative too, celebrating the context. The home occupies the place of the family's earlier abode, a rambling 22-room structure, which also functioned as their office, standing next to a small well. The client had purchased it from a Parsi gentleman, complete with beautiful wooden furniture. While the rooms were numerous, they were tiny, and the spatial orchestration was not at all user-friendly. Plus, with ageing family members, particularly one who is physically challenged as well, the need to shift to a modern home with an inclusive, barrier-free design became crucial and pressing.

item.title: Les Feixes Becomes the Setting for a Film Exploring Architecture and Geometry
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description: On Spain's Costa Brava, the little-known brutalist housing block Les Feixes, in L'Estartit, becomes the main stage of "Caçador de Geometries" (Geometry Hunter), a short film produced by Simon and directed by filmmaker Matilda Vidal de Llobatera. Its premiere marks the launch of the sixth edition of the Living Places – Simon Architecture Prize, the only award that uses video to explain architecture from the perspective of those who inhabit it. Curated by Fundació Mies van der Rohe since 2016, it is now open and, coinciding with its tenth anniversary, it joins the program of Barcelona 2026, World Capital of Architecture.

item.title: Oslo Architecture Triennale 2026 Announces Programme for 9th Edition Under "What if Nature Comes First?"
item.dc:creator: Reyyan Dogan
item.description: The 2026 Oslo Architecture Triennale will take place from September 17 to October 1 at Sofienberg Church in Oslo, bringing together more than 30 international architecture projects around the question "What if Nature Comes First?" For its ninth edition, the Triennale will adopt a two-week festival format, combining an exhibition with conferences, seminars, workshops, film screenings and guided walks. Curated by Line Ramstad, the programme will examine how placing nature at the starting point of architectural decision-making could influence what is built, preserved, transformed or left untouched.

item.title: Salle de médiation culturelle / atelier iso architectes
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: The building is located within the Moulin des Gourmands, a tourist site dedicated to the discovery and promotion of traditional milling heritage. Operated by the local tourist office, the site welcomes a wide range of visitors throughout the year, including school groups, individual visitors, associations, and organized groups.

item.title: Reused Brick and Timber Shape Reiulf Ramstad Arkitekter's New Railway Station in Sweden
item.dc:creator: Antonia Piñeiro
item.description: Construction is advancing on Gothenburg Grand Central, a new station building and prominent western entrance designed by Reiulf Ramstad Arkitekter. The project is part of the West Link (Västlänken) commuter rail project at Gothenburg Central Station, consisting of 8 kilometers of railway, including three new stations: Centralen, Haga, and Korsvägen. The new route is projected to increase capacity during peak hours and reduce travel times for commuter and regional trains, connecting directly to the existing central station and the Nils Ericson Terminal. The new station is scheduled to open alongside Västlänken's Centralen underground station in December 2026, with office tenants moving in during 2027, and the rest of the tunnel planned to be ready for traffic by December 2030.

item.title: Ephemeral Architecture Prototypes: The Future of Public Spaces
item.dc:creator: Olivia Poston
item.description: Concéntrico returned to Logroño for its 12th edition in June 2026, transforming the city into a working site for architecture. Since its founding in 2015, the festival has built an identity on resisting a distant, controlled exhibition of design by constructing full-scale installations in the city's streets, plazas, and vacant lots. Concéntrico embeds installations directly into daily life, engaging residents and visitors as active, observant participants. This year's program brought together more than twenty projects by architects, designers, and researchers working across geographies and methods, each contributing to a citywide experiment in reimagining public space.

item.title: Tomi House / The Studio
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: Tomi House is built on a 4 × 15.5-meter plot within an existing residential neighborhood in Quy Nhon, Vietnam. Shaped by the constraints of a narrow and deep townhouse, the project brings natural light, ventilation, and everyday family life into the center of the house through its spatial organization.

item.title: DR House / ARC Architects
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: Located on the north-eastern outskirts of Tashkent, the house sits between two contrasting environments. The site is accessible from two streets, with a canal and gardens on one side and a low-rise residential neighborhood, or mahalla, on the other. The house was positioned to open toward the gardens, while the upper floors offered views of the surrounding landscape and, on clear days, the mountains beyond.

item.title: Ouse Fashion Lobby / say architects
item.dc:creator: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang
item.description: Ouse Fashion is rooted in Hangzhou, with two decades dedicated to one craft: tailoring the warmth of life into clothing. For them, fashion is not merely about appearance — it is about the ease with which one inhabits their daily life. A corporate lobby is the first point of contact between people and a brand. Employees walk in every day and need to feel a sense of purpose in their work. First-time visitors — the materials, the light, the scale — already speak of the brand's taste and standards. Partners step in, and the lobby should emit a signal of an entire aesthetic system.

item.title: Raw & Warm Residence / Habitat Architects
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: Raw & Warm was conceived as a residential laboratory for an art collector—a home where architecture, art, and daily life could coexist without competing for attention. Rather than concealing the original structure, the design preserves the exposed concrete ceiling and its irregular texture, allowing the building's raw character to become the starting point of the spatial narrative.

item.title: The Threshold House / Madras Spaces
item.dc:creator: Pratik Mour
item.description: Located in V. Thuraiyur, near Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, this 1000 sq.ft farmhouse by Madras Spaces is conceived as a quiet return to a lost native landscape. Set amidst agricultural fields and far removed from urban noise, the project responds to a tight site, limited resources, and a brief rooted more in memory and belonging than in program.

item.title: Cuattro Casa de Café / Faci Leboreiro
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: At Cuattro Casa de Café, the project did not begin by defining the shape of the building, but rather by establishing what had to remain. Located in Troncones, Guerrero, on a sloping 50-by-24-meter lot just minutes from the sea, the brief brought together a café-restaurant, an artisanal bakery, a Mexican handcrafts shop, and a private office under one determining condition: to preserve all existing vegetation and respond to the tropical climate primarily through passive strategies.

item.title: Zimbro House / Stemmer Rodrigues Arquitetura
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: Casa Zimbro was born from the search for an architecture in continuity with the landscape, where the construction does not impose itself on its surroundings but rather integrates with them in a natural and sensitive way. Sited between the lake and the garden, the house is designed in a light and welcoming manner, shaping itself as a refuge that invites both contemplation and gathering.

item.title: Nooba Building / Saraiva + Associados
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: Located on the south bank of the Tagus River in Barreiro, Nooba is conceived as a new residential neighborhood shaped by its proximity to the estuary and the profound urban transformation underway in the south bank's former industrial areas. The project occupies a strategic position within a broad process of urban and environmental regeneration, where new public spaces, mobility infrastructure, and ecological corridors redefine the city's relationship with the river. Its planning framework responds to this metropolitan condition by proposing a neighborhood that balances density with openness, positioning housing as the driver of daily urban life and reinforcing continuity with the revitalized waterfront.

item.title: Zamalanda Park on the Nervión Riverbanks / Burgos & Garrido arquitectos
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: The area surrounding the Portu Dock in Barakaldo is a vast, empty space that bears the traces of its history. Although blurred, it is a place of great beauty and extraordinary potential, offering splendid views over the Nervión estuary from its upper level and a lush, wild horizontal landscape on its lower level.

item.title: The Public Kitchen: How Asian Markets Turn Eating Into Civic Life
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Yeung
item.description: In many Asian cities, eating has never belonged entirely to the private home. It spills into markets, hawker centers, street stalls, and wholesale districts embedded within larger buildings or areas. These are places where the city exchanges information and watches other people pass through. They are not restaurants in the conventional sense, nor are they simply markets. In some way, their vibrancy and usage reflect the society's conditions at that moment. They are public kitchens: shared infrastructures where domestic routines are partially transferred into collective space.

item.title: Housing on top of the petrol station / Gut Deubelbeiss Nill Architekten
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: The project is situated in Emmenbrücke, a town just outside Lucerne. Set within an industrial and high-traffic environment, the building marks the start of the row of houses by Emmenbrücke railway station. Nestled between the railway tracks and the main road, the ground floor houses a petrol station, while the six stories above provide residential apartments.
